questions.explanation: A correct answer follows from the view's central commitment, not from a side remark. Consequentialism judges acts by the value of their outcomes. This is the position defended by John Stuart Mill. The claim that consequentialism judges acts by their intrinsic character alone is a common mistake about the view, often described as "confuses consequentialism with act-independent deontology". A fair assessment also has to reckon with this worry: it may permit sacrificing the innocent. Keeping the thesis and this mistake distinct is the point of the item.
